prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: מערכת שעות כיתת י'2 – סמסטר א' (language he, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "ראשון" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שני" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שלישי" spans 1 col × 3 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "יום" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
  col 2: header "שעה" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 89px
  col 3: header "מקצוע" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 63px
  col 4: header "מורה" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 68px
  col 5: header "חדר" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 76px
  col 6: header "הערות" · longest unbreakable word 64px · one-line width 700px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"poor","why":"Hour column is too narrow, so every time range breaks after the dash (08:15– / 09:00), disrupting the main scan; notes also wrap tightly."},"B":{"grade":"good","why":"Balanced and readable: times stay on one line and key columns hold; notes are slightly tighter than in D, with more wrapping."},"C":{"grade":"bad","why":"Notes are crushed into a narrow strip, one or two words per line, making the table extremely tall while other columns sit mostly empty."},"D":{"grade":"excellent","why":"Best proportion: times, subjects, teachers and rooms remain scannable, while notes get enough width for readable multi-line blocks; rows have an even rhythm."},"E":{"grade":"poor","why":"Teacher names and room labels break across lines in most rows, making the schedule busy and harder to scan; notes are cramped."},"F":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"Times and notes are usable, but room identifiers such as מעבדה 1 split across lines and the allocation is less clean than D/B."}},"best":["D"],"confidence":"medium","unsure":"Exact column widths are hard to measure from screenshots; B and D are close, and some room/teacher wraps are borderline."}
